questions.question: An inference is a conclusion reached by combining clues with what?
Textual evidence is information taken from where?
“Wet footprints crossed the kitchen, and an open umbrella leaned by the door.” What is a reasonable inference?
choices: someone came inside from the rain

questions.question: A character rereads a letter, folds it carefully, and puts it away. What can readers reasonably infer?
choices: the letter is definitely a bill
the letter may be important to the character

questions.question: Which statement is best supported by a text showing a town adding benches and shade to a public plaza?
choices: the town will become a major city
the town is making the plaza more comfortable for visitors
the plaza is open all night

questions.question: A passage says a researcher repeated a test and got similar results. What inference is supported?
choices: the result is certainly true in every case
the result may be more consistent than a single trial

questions.question: A student claims a character is generous. Which evidence is strongest?
choices: the character shares supplies with a new student
the character owns a large backpack
another character has a different name

questions.question: Which is an inference rather than a directly stated fact?
choices: The character may be worried because she checks the clock repeatedly.

questions.question: A text reports that a shop’s sales rose after it extended its hours. What can readers infer cautiously?
choices: longer hours may have contributed to the increase
longer hours were the only cause

questions.question: A character says “I’m fine,” avoids eye contact, and leaves quickly after criticism. What is a reasonable inference?
A passage states a bridge closed after inspectors found cracks. Which conclusion is supported?
choices: safety concerns led to the closure
the bridge was built last year

questions.question: A reader cites a sentence that does not address the claim. What is the issue?
choices: the inference uses too many words
the evidence is not relevant to the inference

questions.question: A student says “the speaker is angry” because the speaker uses a raised voice once. What additional evidence would strengthen the inference?
choices: repeated hostile words or actions across the passage

questions.question: A passage says attendance improved after a bus route changed, but does not mention other factors. What inference is appropriately cautious?
choices: the route change caused every improvement
the route change may have helped attendance

questions.question: A character returns a borrowed tool clean and repaired. Which trait is best supported?
A text describes a garden with dry soil, drooping leaves, and a broken irrigation hose. Which inference is best supported?
choices: the plants may not be receiving enough water

questions.question: A reader notices a claim has two supporting details and one exception. What should a strong interpretation do?
choices: account for both the support and the exception
treat one detail as proof of everything

questions.question: Which pairing best connects inference and evidence?
choices: “She is famous” supported by her blue coat
“He is kind” supported by his name
“She may be nervous” supported by her shaking hands
“They are lost” supported by a sunny day

questions.question: A passage says a student practiced each afternoon and gradually improved on timed reading. What conclusion is best supported?
choices: regular practice may have contributed to improvement
practice guarantees top scores for everyone
reading speed is fixed at birth

questions.question: An inference conflicts with a clear sentence in the passage. What should a reader do?
choices: keep it because all interpretations are equal
revise the inference to fit the text
